title: The scheduler decides inside a container that holds no host tool and acts only through the executor, a dumb host process behind gRPC on a unix socket; the socket is the control plane and stays
text: Rejected: a container with the home directory mounted (every host tool bound in); the scheduler typing into a shell pane (prompt parsing, no exit code); the scheduler on the host (not Podman). Cost: two processes, two panes, one socket. Revised 2026-10-13 (card C15): the title used to say the bus later replaces the socket, and the node depended on DEC-nats-jetstream-grpc. With NATS deferred and the bus a set of files in the state root, the unix socket is the control plane only, never the bus, so it stays whatever the bus becomes, and the depends_on edge to the NATS decision is removed.
